title: Design System: Break the Bonds | Arkansas

poster.purpose: The home title only, sized from Lalezar's measured widths so the longest line fills the measure; three lines on phones at clamp(3.5rem, calc((100vw - 2.25rem) / 5.6), 7.5rem), two from 60rem.

display.purpose: Poster-band titles on Persuade pages, institution headings, the 404 title. 14ch max.

display-read.purpose: Poster-band titles on Read pages, smaller so the record starts higher. 16ch max.

headline.purpose: Section headings set as poster lines: splits, chapters, win rows, the close-strip line.

title.purpose: Default h2, source headings, timeline and due-strip titles. Lalezar also sets every money figure.

button.purpose: Button labels: printed blocks of ink.

body.purpose: Reading copy at a 30em measure, lining numerals.

small.purpose: Provenance, tables, captions, scope notes; olive ink.

dateline.purpose: Datelines and margin labels; in the 12rem margin on Read pages, under the heading on phones.

data.purpose: Record IDs, CUSIPs, ISO dates, hashes, the timeline year axis. Never a costume.

shadows.name: focus-ring-on-paper
shadows.purpose: Second ring around the 3px ink focus outline (offset 3px) on paper. The only box-shadow; marks focus, never depth.

shadows.name: focus-ring-on-ink-grounds
shadows.purpose: On olive and red the inks swap: paper outline, ink ring. An ink button on red keeps an ink outline with a paper ring.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing for every transition and the register moment.

motion.name: register
motion.value: translate(0.06em, -0.035em) to none, 900ms ease-out, 120ms delay, backwards fill
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the red "out of" in the home title drops into register with the olive sheet. Off under forced colours; 1ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: state-nudge
motion.purpose: Go-link arrows (0.15em), record-row arrows (0.3rem), disclosure plus (45deg).

motion.name: tellbar-scroll
motion.purpose: Phone Tell bar stays hidden over the first screen, then slides in; appears without sliding under reduced motion. No JavaScript.

breakpoints.name: phone-max
breakpoints.purpose: Tables reflow into slips, Tell bar shows, timeline drawing hides.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Footer goes three columns, the ATRS money steps go four across, masthead nav runs as one row up to 64rem.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Margin grid, splits, two-line poster title, multi-column rows.

breakpoints.name: masthead
breakpoints.purpose: Masthead is a single row from here; below, a brand/action grid with nav beneath.

narrative.northStar: The Poster and Its Fine Print
narrative.overview:
Each page opens as a silkscreened solidarity poster from the Palestinian poster tradition: flat ink pulled in one pass, one message per sheet, type knocked out of the colour. The Arkansas records sit under the poster as the fine print it stands on. The poster states the demand at a scale meant to be read across a room. The records below are dated, sourced, and set for close reading, because reporters and skeptics will check them.

The world has three inks and paper. Deep olive covers the poster sheet, and paper-white type is knocked out of it. Mark red, taken from the campaign mark, is held back for what is due or being asked now. Black ink sets the record on a cool lime-wash paper. Tints are halftone screens of olive dots, never washes. Lalezar, from Arabic-script poster and cinema lettering, carries the display voice. Markazi Text, drawn for Arabic and Latin together, sets the reading copy. Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono sets record IDs, CUSIPs, ISO dates and hashes, where a reader has to tell 0 from O.

The density is two-speed. The sheet is loud and sparse, with one message, one action and one strip of dates. The record is quiet and dense, with tables, provenance lines, rules and margins. The system refuses the campaign template of a dark band, a red eyebrow and an italic-serif second line, and it refuses the soft-cornered NGO report.
keyCharacteristics: Every page opens on the olive sheet: a full poster on the home page, a poster band with breadcrumb on every other page.
Three inks and paper, printed flat. No shadows, no gradient fills, no rounded corners.
Red means "due now" or "asked now", and nothing else.
Headings carry their own weight. Nothing is printed above a heading.
Every figure carries its date and record beside it.
Rules, bars and squares are the structure. Boxes and cards are not.

rules.name: The Due-Now Rule
rules.body: Red marks only what is due or being asked now: the primary action, the fall maturities, the demand, and links that lead to the ask. If an element is neither the ask nor a date that is due, it is not red. Red is never used for emphasis, decoration, status or error.

rules.name: The Ink-of-Its-Ground Rule
rules.body: Links underline in the ink of the ground they sit on: olive at 60% on paper, Second Pull on olive, ink on red. Only links that carry the ask underline in red: anything pointing to /take-action/, `tel:` links, and artreasury.gov links. They use Dense Mark Red on paper and Mark Red on olive.

rules.name: The Never-Gray Rule
rules.body: Secondary text on paper is olive ink. On olive it is Second Pull. No gray exists in the system.

rules.name: The One-Ink Heading Rule
rules.body: On paper a heading prints in one ink. Only on the olive sheet does the heading's second line take the second ink, Second Pull. On red it stays ink. Emphasis is a change of ink. It is never a slant, a second face or a synthesized heavier weight, because Lalezar has one weight (400).

rules.name: The Margin Dateline Rule
rules.body: No label, eyebrow, kicker or section number is printed above a heading. On Read pages, datelines and record IDs sit in the 12rem left margin beside the heading. On phones they sit under the heading. A page's own label is the last item of its breadcrumb.

rules.name: The Figure-and-Record Rule
rules.body: A money figure is set in Lalezar, and its record line (date and source, in Small olive ink) prints directly beside or beneath it. A figure never appears without its record line.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Records Rule
rules.body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono is used only where characters must be told apart: IDs, CUSIPs, ISO dates, hashes and measurement axes. It is never a "technical" costume.

rules.name: The One-Sheet Rule
rules.body: The olive sheet appears once per page, at the top. Further down the page, rules and halftone screens divide sections, and red fields carry the ask. The olive is not repeated as a mid-page band.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading text holds a 30em measure. Display lines may run the full width, but prose may not.

rules.name: The One-Pass Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. Layers are inks laid flat, never elevations. A block needs a different ink, a screen or a rule to stand apart, not a shadow.

dos: Do open every page on the olive sheet: the full poster on the home page, and the poster band with breadcrumb, title and intro everywhere else.
Do keep red for the ask and what is due now, with Mark Red (#ff5b4f) on olive and as fields, and Dense Mark Red (#c42b22) for text on paper.
Do print the second line of a heading in Second Pull (#b9c49a) only on the olive sheet. On paper and red, a heading is one ink.
Do print every money figure in Lalezar with its date and source beside it in olive-ink Small type.
Do put datelines and record IDs in the 12rem margin on Read pages, under the heading on phones.
Do hold reading text to the 30em measure and every target to at least 2.75rem.
Do separate blocks with the rule weights (0.75rem bar, 3px, 2px, 1px hairline) and tint only with the olive halftone screen.
Do theme the browser surfaces from the inks: red selection with ink text, olive-on-paper scrollbars, the two-ink focus ring, and the 0.18em underline offset.
Do keep forced colours, print and reduced motion working: in print everything goes black on white, disclosures print open, and link URLs are printed.
donts: Don't print a label, eyebrow, kicker or section number above a heading.
Don't use red for emphasis, decoration, status, errors or ordinary links.
Don't slant heading emphasis, set it in a second face, or give paper headings a second ink.
Don't add shadows, rounded corners, gradients other than the halftone screen, glass, or a second olive band mid-page.
Don't use gray. Secondary text is olive ink on paper and Second Pull on olive.
Don't use monospace outside IDs, CUSIPs, ISO dates, hashes and measurement axes.
Don't turn statuses into badges, pills or coloured chips. They print as words.
Don't use photographs, stock or generated imagery. Images are literal crops of source records on a halftone mount.
Don't use Unicode glyphs or emoji as icons. Use the drawn 24-unit, 2-stroke set.
Don't rewrite body copy to fit a layout. The body copy reproduces the old site word for word, so fit the layout to the copy.
